title: "Supporting Information 4"
author: "Daniel Y.M. Nakamura, Ward C. Wheeler, Taran Grant"
date: "2026-06-15"
output: html_document
---

To test the assumption that morphological partitions would be swamped by genomic partitions, we compiled a diverse array of 63 published datasets and evaluated the impact of morphological evidence in both maximum likelihood (ML) and maximum parsimony (MP) analyses. Specifically, we addressed the following questions: (1) Do MOL and TE topologies differ? (2) Are distances between MOL and TE topologies related to the proportion of morphological characters? (3) Do the effects of morphological evidence on topology and optimality scores differ between maximum likelihood (ML) and maximum parsimony (MP) analyses? (4) Does morphological evidence affect the support values of clades shared by MOL and TE trees? (5) Do support values of MOL clades predict the occurrence of those clades in TE trees?

# Exploratory analyses

## Distributions of characters (Figure S1)

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")

# Panel A
p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = nMolCharacters)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, color = "black", fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Number of molecular characters",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Panel B
p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = nMorphCharacters)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, color = "black", fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Number of morphological characters",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Panel C
p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X.Morph.Total)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    color = "black",
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_scientific()) +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion of morphological characters",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Panel D
p4 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = nTEterminals)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 30, color = "black", fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Number of terminals",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Combine panels
fig <- (p1 | p2) /
       (p3 | p4) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.tag.position = c(0.02, 0.98)
  )

# Save as JPEG (300 dpi)
ggsave(
  "Figures/S1_histograms.jpg",
  fig,
  width = 8,
  height = 8,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Year x Size (Figure 10)

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")

# Panel A
# Fit model
lm_exp <- lm(log(nMolCharacters) ~ Year, data = df)
# Prediction grid
newdat <- data.frame(
  Year = seq(min(df$Year), max(df$Year), length.out = 200)
)
# Predictions with 95% confidence intervals
pred <- predict(lm_exp, newdata = newdat, interval = "confidence")
newdat$fit <- exp(pred[, "fit"])
newdat$lwr <- exp(pred[, "lwr"])
newdat$upr <- exp(pred[, "upr"])
# Plot
p1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = df,
    aes(Year, nMolCharacters),
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8,
    color = "steelblue"
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = newdat,
    aes(x = Year, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr),
    fill = "grey70",
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = newdat,
    aes(x = Year, y = fit),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "No. molecular characters"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Panel B
p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Year, y = nMorphCharacters)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "No. morphological characters"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Panel C
p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Year, y = X.Morph.Total)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_scientific()) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "% Morphological characters"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Panel D
p4 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Year, y = nTEterminals)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "No. terminals"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Combine panels
fig <- (p1 | p2) /
       (p3 | p4) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "plain"),
    plot.tag.position = c(0.02, 0.98)
  )

# Save figure
ggsave(
  "Figures/Fig10_yearXsize.jpg",
  fig,
  width = 8,
  height = 8,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```


# Q1. Are topologies impacted by the addition of morphological evidence?

Dataset with MOL-TE topological distances were calculated in script 1.

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
extinct_datasets <- unique(df$Dataset[df$Type == "Extinct"])
# Append the extant datasets that do not appear among extinct
df_extinct <- df[df$Type == "Extinct" | 
                  (df$Type == "Extant" & !(df$Dataset %in% extinct_datasets)), ]

print("EXTANT: Number of datasets (extant) impacted by the addition of morphological evidence")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets
print("MP MOL vs MP TE (number min)")
sum(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF > 0) 
print("MP MOL vs MP TE (proportion min)")
sum(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF > 0) / nrow(df_extant) 
print("MP MOL vs MP TE (number strict)")
sum(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus > 0)
```

## Q1.2 Statistical tests

### Q1.2.1 Extant (Table S3)

To test if MOL-TE incongruences are significantly different from zero, we can check if the distribution of observed values are significantly different from zero. 

For each comparison and for each topological distance metric, we tested for normality. Because data are not normal according to Shapiro-Wilk tests (P < 0.05 in all cases), we tested if the median of each topological distance metric is different from zero using a non-parametric Wilcoxon Signed-Ranked test. First, the V statistic is computed by summing the signed ranks of the differences between the observed values and the hypothesized value (i.e. zero). The ranks are assigned based on the absolute values of the differences, and the sign is determined by whether the original value is positive or negative. Second, given that the distribution of V values is normally distributed for a large sample size due to the Central Limit Theorem, P-values can be calculated by finding the area under the normal curve corresponding to the calculated Z-score.

Using minimum values of topological distances:

```{r}
print("1a. MPmol vs MPte")
print("Minimum RF")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1a_rf <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1a_rf
print("Minimum CID")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID))  # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1a_cid <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1a_cid
print("Minimum SPR")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1a_spr <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1a_spr
print("Strict RF")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1a_rf <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1a_rf
print("Strict CID")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus))  # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1a_cid <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1a_cid

print("1b. MLmol vs MLteAsc")
print("RF")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1b_rf <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1b_rf
print("CID")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1b_cid <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1b_cid
print("SPR")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1b_spr <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1b_spr

print("1c. MLmol vs MLteNoAsc")
print("RF")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1c_rf <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1c_rf
print("CID")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1c_cid <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1c_cid
print("SPR")
shapiro.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR)) # non-parametric, p < 0.05
q1c_spr <- wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR), mu = 0, exact=F, conf.int=T)
q1c_spr
```

In all cases, the median of normalized RF, CID, and SPR values in MP and ML are significantly different from zero. Thus, MOL-TE incongruences different from zero indicate that the morphological evidence tends to impact topologies in empirical studies.

### Q1.3.3 Proportion of affected clades (Figure S5)

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets
#df_extinct <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extinct", Type)) # keep only extinct datasets
# Keep only extinct
extinct_datasets <- unique(df$Dataset[df$Type == "Extinct"])
# Append the extant datasets that do not appear among extinct
df_extinct <- df[df$Type == "Extinct" | 
                  (df$Type == "Extant" & !(df$Dataset %in% extinct_datasets)), ]

# Format data
df_plot <- tibble(
  Method = c(
    rep("MP", 2 * nrow(df_extant)),
    rep("ML (Mk)", 2 * nrow(df_extant)),
    rep("ML (MkV)", 2 * nrow(df_extant))
  ),
  Dataset = c(
    rep(c("MOL", "TE"), each = nrow(df_extant)),
    rep(c("MOL", "TE"), each = nrow(df_extant)),
    rep(c("MOL", "TE"), each = nrow(df_extant))
  ),
  Proportion = c(
    df_extant$MP_nUniqueCladesMOL / df_extant$MP_MOL_nClades,
    df_extant$MP_nUniqueCladesTE / df_extant$MP_TE_nClades,

    df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_nUniqueCladesMOL /
      df_extant$ML_MOL_nClades,
    df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_nUniqueCladesTEnoASC /
      df_extant$ML_TE_noASC_nClades,

    df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_nUniqueCladesMOL /
      df_extant$ML_MOL_nClades,
    df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_nUniqueCladesTEASC /
      df_extant$ML_TE_ASC_nClades
  )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Proportion))


# MP
df_extant$MP_nUniqueCladesMOL / df_extant$MP_MOL_nClades
df_extant$MP_nUniqueCladesTE / df_extant$MP_TE_nClades

# ML MK
df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_nUniqueCladesMOL / df_extant$ML_MOL_nClades
df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_nUniqueCladesTEnoASC / df_extant$ML_TE_noASC_nClades

# ML MKv
df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_nUniqueCladesMOL / df_extant$ML_MOL_nClades
df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_nUniqueCladesTEASC / df_extant$ML_TE_ASC_nClades

# Wilcoxon
pvals <- df_plot %>%
  group_by(Method, Dataset) %>%
  summarise(
    p = wilcox.test(Proportion, mu = 0)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    label = paste0("P = ", format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-16))
  )

# Figure S5
fig <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Proportion)) +
  geom_density(
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.5,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_grid(Dataset ~ Method) +
  geom_text(
    data = pvals,
    aes(
      x = Inf,
      y = Inf,
      label = label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1.05,
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion of unique clades",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "plain")
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "Figures/FigS5_uniqueClades_density.jpg",
  plot = fig,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

# Q2.Are MOL-TE incongruences associated with the proportion of morphological characters? 

## Q2.1 Spearman correlations

To test if the proportion of morphological characters is associated with the topological metrics of MOL-TE incongruences, we used a non-parametric Spearman's Rank Correlation test. The rho values measure the association between two variables based on their rank orders: a rho of +1 indicates a perfect monotonic increasing relationship; a rho of -1 indicates a perfect monotonic decreasing relationship; a rho of zero indicates a no monotonic relationship.

### Q2.1.1 Extant (Table 3)

```{r, warning=F}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets

print("Minimum RF: MP MOL vs MP TE")
cor.test(df_extant$X.Morph.Total, df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF, method = "spearman")
plot_mp_rf_min = ggplot(df_extant, aes(x = X.Morph.Total, y = MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF)) +
  geom_point() +  # scatter plot
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "#339999", se = T) +  # regression line (lm) for the trend
  stat_cor(method = "spearman", label.x = 0.075, label.y = 0.6) +  # add Spearman correlation value
  theme_minimal()+
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL)

print("Strict RF: MP MOL vs MP TE")
cor.test(df_extant$X.Morph.Total, df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus, method = "spearman")
plot_mp_rf_strict = ggplot(df_extant, aes(x = X.Morph.Total, y = MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus)) +
  geom_point() +  # scatter plot
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "#335100", se = T) +  # regression line (lm) for the trend
  stat_cor(method = "spearman", label.x = 0.075, label.y = 0.6) +  # add Spearman correlation value
  theme_minimal()+
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL)

print("Minimum CID: MP MOL vs MP TE")
cor.test(df_extant$X.Morph.Total, df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID, method = "spearman")
```

### Q2.1.2 Extant + extinct (Table 3)

To test if the proportion of morphological characters is associated with the topological metrics of MOL-TE incongruences, we used a non-parametric Spearman's Rank Correlation test. The rho values measure the association between two variables based on their rank orders: a rho of +1 indicates a perfect monotonic increasing relationship; a rho of -1 indicates a perfect monotonic decreasing relationship; a rho of zero indicates a no monotonic relationship.

```{r, warning=F}

# Append the extant datasets that do not appear among extinct
```

```{r}
custom_palette <- c("MPmol_MPte_min" = "#339999",

)

legend_df <- data.frame(
  comparison = factor(
    c("MPmol_MPte_min","MPmol_MPte_strict","MLmol_MLteAsc","MLmol_MLteNoAsc"),
    levels = c("MPmol_MPte_min","MPmol_MPte_strict","MLmol_MLteAsc","MLmol_MLteNoAsc")
  ),
  value = 1
)

legend <- ggplot(legend_df, aes(x = comparison, y = value, color = comparison)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
```

### Q2.2.3 %Morphology-only taxa vs RF/CID/SPR (Figure S7)

```{r}
# Proportion of fossils vs RF/CID/SPR distances

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ggpubr)

# 1. Map your custom palette to the Method strings used in the dataframe
custom_palette <- c(
  "ML Mkv"    = "#6f77b4", # MLmol_MLteAsc
  "ML Mk"     = "#cccccc", # MLmol_MLteNoAsc
  "MP (min)"  = "#339999", # MPmol_MPte_min
  "MP strict" = "#335100"  # MPmol_MPte_strict
)

# Proportion of fossils vs RF/CID/SPR distances

# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extinct <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extinct", Type)) # keep only extant datasets

# Create new column
df_extinct$percentageFossils <- df_extinct$nUniqueMorphTerminals / df_extinct$nTEterminals

# Convert to long format
df_long <- bind_rows(
  
  # RF
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF, Method = "MP (min)", Metric = "RF"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus, Method = "MP strict", Metric = "RF"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF, Method = "ML Mk", Metric = "RF"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF, Method = "ML Mkv", Metric = "RF"),
  
  # CID
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID, Method = "MP (min)", Metric = "CID"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus, Method = "MP strict", Metric = "CID"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID, Method = "ML Mk", Metric = "CID"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, Method = "ML Mkv", Metric = "CID"),
  
  # SPR
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR, Method = "MP (min)", Metric = "SPR"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR, Method = "ML Mk", Metric = "SPR"),
  tibble(percentageFossils = df_extinct$percentageFossils, Distance = df_extinct$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR, Method = "ML Mkv", Metric = "SPR")
  
) %>%
  drop_na(Distance, percentageFossils)

# Updated make_panel function
make_panel <- function(metric, method, ylim=NULL, 
                       show_x=FALSE, show_y=FALSE, show_title=FALSE){
  
  d <- filter(df_long, Metric==metric, Method==method)
  
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = percentageFossils, y = Distance)) +
    geom_point(color = custom_palette[[method]], size=2, alpha=0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE, color="black") +
    # Move P-value and R2 to the upper right corner (hjust=1 prevents clipping)
    stat_cor(method="spearman", label.x.npc = 0.95, label.y.npc = 0.98, hjust = 1, size = 3) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,1), ylim=ylim) +
    labs(
      x = if(show_x) "% Morphology-only terminals" else NULL,
      y = if(show_y) paste("Normalized", metric) else NULL
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size=12) +
    ggtitle(if(show_title) method else NULL) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust=.5, size=12, face="bold"),
      axis.title.x = if(show_x) element_text(size=12) else element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = if(show_y) element_text(size=12) else element_blank()
    )
  
  if(!show_x) p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
  if(!show_y) p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  
  p
}

###########################################################
# Blank panel (MP strict × SPR)
###########################################################

# Empty subset panel for the missing SPR data, keeps X-axis aligned on bottom row
blank_panel <- make_panel("SPR", "MP strict", ylim=c(0,1), 
                          show_x=TRUE, show_y=FALSE, show_title=FALSE) +
               theme(panel.border = element_rect(fill=NA, color="grey50"))


###########################################################
# Row 1 : RF (Columns: ML Mkv, ML Mk, MP (min), MP strict)
###########################################################

p11 <- make_panel("RF", "ML Mkv",
                  ylim=range(filter(df_long, Metric=="RF", Method=="ML Mkv")$Distance, na.rm=TRUE),
                  show_y=TRUE, show_title=TRUE)

p12 <- make_panel("RF", "ML Mk",
                  ylim=range(filter(df_long, Metric=="RF", Method=="ML Mk")$Distance, na.rm=TRUE),
                  show_title=TRUE)

p13 <- make_panel("RF", "MP (min)", 
                  ylim=range(filter(df_long, Metric=="RF", Method=="MP (min)")$Distance, na.rm=TRUE),
                  show_title=TRUE)

p14 <- make_panel("RF", "MP strict",
                  ylim=range(filter(df_long, Metric=="RF", Method=="MP strict")$Distance, na.rm=TRUE),
                  show_title=TRUE)


###########################################################
# Row 2 : CID (Columns: ML Mkv, ML Mk, MP (min), MP strict)
###########################################################

p21 <- make_panel("CID", "ML Mkv",    ylim=c(0,0.30), show_y=TRUE)
p22 <- make_panel("CID", "ML Mk",     ylim=c(0,0.30))
p23 <- make_panel("CID", "MP (min)",  ylim=c(0,0.35))
```

# Q3. Is the addition of morphological evidence equally impactful on ML and MP topologies?

## Q3.1 MOL-TE incongruences ~ Optimality criteria

To test whether the MOL-TE incongruences are different between ML and MP, we first need to change the structure of the dataframe.

### Q3.1.1 Extant (Table 4)

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets

# Create an empty data frame for RF
q3_rf <- data.frame(value = numeric(0), source = character(0))
# Combine the vectors of RF into the data frame
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_min", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF))))
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMeanRF, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_strict", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus))))
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF))))
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEnoASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF))))
# Summary of medians
q3_rf %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value = min(value, na.rm=T),
    max_value = max(value, na.rm=T),
    n = n())

# Create an empty data frame for CID
q3_cid <- data.frame(value = numeric(0), source = character(0))
# Combine the vectors of CID into the data frame
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_min", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID))))
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMeanCID, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_strict", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus))))
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID))))
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEnoASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID))))
# Summary of medians
q3_cid %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value = min(value, na.rm=T),
    max_value = max(value, na.rm=T),
    n = n())

# Create an empty data frame for SPR
q3_spr <- data.frame(value = numeric(0), source = character(0))
# Combine the vectors of CID into the data frame
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_min", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR))))
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR))))
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEnoASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR))))
# Summary of medians
q3_spr %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value = min(value, na.rm=T),
    max_value = max(value, na.rm=T),
    n = n())
```

Then, we statistically test whether MOL-TE incongruences (operationally measured as normalized RF, CID, and SPR) differ between (1) MP MOL vs TE, (2) ML MOL vs TE MKv (with bias correction), and (3) ML MOL vs TE MK (no bias correction). Because data are not normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk tests: P < 0.05) and more than one category is present in the predictor variable, we performed the following tests:

- The Kruskal-Wallis test is a nonparametric test used to compare the medians (or ranks) between >2 groups. As assumptions, this test does not require normality and observations must be independent. First, data is ranked (from the lowest to the highest value) and the mean rank computed. Next, we compute the statistic H (differences between group mean ranks and the overall mean rank, scaled by sample size). Finally, p-values can be estimated by comparing the statistic H and chi-squared distribution (if H is large, the p-value will be small).

- The Friedman test is a nonparametric test used to compare ordinal or continuous values that are paired between >2 groups. As assumptions, this test does not require normality and observations can be dependent (paired). First, ranks are assigned to the pairwise structure across groups. Next, the average rank within group is computed. The Friedman statistic measures how far group rank sums deviate from the expected value in the null model. Finally, p-values are computed by comparing the Friedman statistic and chi-squared distribution.

- The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is a nonparametric test used to compare the ordinal or continuous values between 2 groups (e.g. as posthoc analysis of Friedman tests). As assumptions, this test does not require normality and observations can be dependent. First, all values are ranked. The number of times that a value from one group precedes a value from the other is computed, generating the U statistic (the number of pairwise wins of one group over the other). Next, U is standardized to a normal distribution to obtain the p-value.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
print("RF")
shapiro.test(q3_rf$value) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
print("Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric test for multiple groups (non-paired values)")
kruskal.test(q3_rf$value ~ q3_rf$source)
print("Friedman: non-parametric test for paired values and multiple groups")
q3_rf_fri = data.frame(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF, df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF)
friedman.test(as.matrix(q3_rf_fri))
print("Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values")
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(q3_rf_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(q3_rf_fri), each = nrow(q3_rf_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

print("CID")
shapiro.test(q3_cid$value) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
print("Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric test for multiple groups")
kruskal.test(q3_cid$value ~ q3_cid$source)
print("Friedman: non-parametric test for paired values and multiple groups")
q3_cid_fri = data.frame(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID, df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID)
friedman.test(as.matrix(q3_cid_fri))
print("Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values")
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(q3_cid_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(q3_cid_fri), each = nrow(q3_cid_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

print("SPR")
shapiro.test(q3_spr$value) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
print("Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric test for multiple groups")
kruskal.test(q3_spr$value ~ q3_spr$source)
print("Friedman: non-parametric test for paired values and multiple groups")
q3_spr_fri = data.frame(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR)
friedman.test(as.matrix(q3_spr_fri))
print("Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values")
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(q3_spr_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(q3_spr_fri), each = nrow(q3_spr_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")
```

```{r}
  "MP_MOLvsTE_min" = "MP-MOL vs MP-TE",

  "ML_MOLvsTEnoASC" = "ML-MOL vs ML-TE MK"
)

# Boxplot Normalized RF

  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  # Create boxplot without default outliers
  geom_jitter(aes(color = source), alpha = .4, width = 0.2) +  # Add transparent dots
  labs(x = "", y = "Normalized RF\n", tag="A") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +  # Hide legend if not needed
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels)
# Boxplot CID

  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  # Create boxplot without default outliers

  labs(x = "", y = "\nNormalized CID\n", tag="B") +

  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels)
# Boxplot SPR

  labs(x = "", y = "\nNormalized SPR\n", tag="C") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),axis.text.x = element_blank(),legend.position = "none", axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),legend.title = element_blank())+
#theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),legend.position = "none") +  # Hide legend if not needed
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels)
```

### Q3.1.4 Strict consensus

In this approach, SPR distances are not calculated due to the polytomies.

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets

# Create an empty data frame for RF
q3_rf <- data.frame(value = numeric(0), source = character(0))
# Combine the vectors of RF into the data frame
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_min", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF))))
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_strict", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus))))
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF))))
q3_rf <- rbind(q3_rf, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEnoASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF))))
# Summary of medians
q3_rf %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value = min(value, na.rm=T),
    max_value = max(value, na.rm=T),
    n = n())

# Create an empty data frame for CID
q3_cid <- data.frame(value = numeric(0), source = character(0))
# Combine the vectors of CID into the data frame
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_min", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID))))
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_strict", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus))))
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID))))
q3_cid <- rbind(q3_cid, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEnoASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID))))
# Summary of medians
q3_cid %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value = min(value, na.rm=T),
    max_value = max(value, na.rm=T),
    n = n())

# Create an empty data frame for CID
q3_spr <- data.frame(value = numeric(0), source = character(0))
# Combine the vectors of CID into the data frame
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_min", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID))))
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus, source = base::rep("MP_MOLvsTE_strict", length(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus))))
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID))))
q3_spr <- rbind(q3_spr, data.frame(value = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID, source = base::rep("ML_MOLvsTEnoASC", length(df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID))))
# Summary of medians
q3_spr %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value = min(value, na.rm=T),
    max_value = max(value, na.rm=T),
    n = n())

print("RF")
shapiro.test(q3_rf$value) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
print("Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric test for multiple groups (non-paired values)")
kruskal.test(q3_rf$value ~ q3_rf$source)
print("Friedman: non-parametric test for paired values and multiple groups")
q3_rf_fri = data.frame(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF, df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF)
friedman.test(as.matrix(q3_rf_fri))
print("Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values")
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(q3_rf_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(q3_rf_fri), each = nrow(q3_rf_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

print("CID")
shapiro.test(q3_cid$value) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
print("Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric test for multiple groups")
kruskal.test(q3_cid$value ~ q3_cid$source)
print("Friedman: non-parametric test for paired values and multiple groups")
q3_cid_fri = data.frame(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID,  df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID)
friedman.test(as.matrix(q3_cid_fri))
print("Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values")
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(q3_cid_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(q3_cid_fri), each = nrow(q3_cid_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

print("SPR")
shapiro.test(q3_spr$value) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
print("Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric test for multiple groups")
kruskal.test(q3_spr$value ~ q3_spr$source)
print("Friedman: non-parametric test for paired values and multiple groups")
q3_spr_fri = data.frame(df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID,  df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID, df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID)
friedman.test(as.matrix(q3_spr_fri))
print("Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values")
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(q3_cid_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(q3_cid_fri), each = nrow(q3_cid_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")
```

### Q3.1.5 Statistical interaction with size (Table S5)

The goal of this analysis is assessing a possible statistical interaction between proportion of morphological characters and RF/CID/SPR distances between MOL and TE trees across optimality criteria.

```{r}
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets

# Format dataframe
df <- df_extant
df_long <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    Dataset = df_extant$Dataset,
    Morph = df_extant$X.Morph.Total,
    Criterion = "MP_min",
    RF  = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinRF,
    CID = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinCID,
    SPR = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedMinSPR
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = df_extant$Dataset,
    Morph = df_extant$X.Morph.Total,
    Criterion = "MP_strict",
    RF  = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedRF_strictConsensus,
    CID = df_extant$MP_MOLvsTE_NormalizedCID_strictConsensus,
    SPR = NA
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = df_extant$Dataset,
    Morph = df_extant$X.Morph.Total,
    Criterion = "ML_MK",
    RF  = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedRF,
    CID = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedCID,
    SPR = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEnoASC_NormalizedSPR
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = df_extant$Dataset,
    Morph = df_extant$X.Morph.Total,
    Criterion = "ML_MKv",
    RF  = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedRF,
    CID = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedCID,
    SPR = df_extant$ML_MOLvsTEASC_NormalizedSPR
  )
)
df_long$Criterion <- factor(df_long$Criterion)
```

```{r}
# Models RF ~ Criterion and %MorphoCharacters
# With interaction
m_RF <- lmer(
    RF ~ Morph * Criterion + (1 | Dataset),
    data = df_long
)
# Without interaction

    RF ~ Morph + Criterion + (1 | Dataset),
    data = df_long
)

# Model selection

anova(m_RF0, m_RF)

# Best model
print("Best model considering RF as response variable")
summary(m_RF0)

# Pairwise comparisons
print("Pairwise comparisons considering RF as response variable")
emmeans(m_RF0, pairwise ~ Criterion, adjust = "tukey")
```

## Q3.2 Number of polytomies

One importance difference, however, is the fact that trees were always binary in ML trees, whereas the addition of morphological evidence can maintain, increase or decrease resolution of MP trees.

### Q3.2.3 Statistical tests (Figure S8; Table S6)

Is the difference between MOL and TE resolution higher when fossils are incorporated? 

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
# 1. Filter rows where Dataset is duplicated
df_filtered <- df %>%
  filter(Dataset %in% Dataset[duplicated(Dataset)])
# 2. Keep only the relevant columns
df_filtered <- df_filtered %>%
  select(Type, MP_nPolytomiesMOL, MP_nPolytomiesTE)
# 3. Compute paired difference
df_filtered <- df_filtered %>%
  mutate(diff = MP_nPolytomiesTE - MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
# 4. Reshape
df_extant <- df_filtered %>% filter(Type == "Extant")
df_extinct <- df_filtered %>% filter(Type == "Extinct")
n_extant <- nrow(df_extant)
df_extinct <- df_extinct %>% slice(1:n_extant)
df_extinct <- df_extinct %>%
  select(-Type) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_Extinct"))
df_wide <- cbind(df_extant, df_extinct)
df_wide <- df_wide %>% select(-Type)
# Exclude MP_nPolytomiesMOL_Extinct
df_reduced <- df_wide %>%
  select(-MP_nPolytomiesMOL_Extinct)

# 5. Exploratory (Table S6)
print("Median of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (without fossils")
median(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
print("SD of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (without fossils")
sd(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
print("Min of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (without fossils")
min(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
print("Max of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (without fossils")
max(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)

print("Median of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (with fossils")
median(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
print("SD of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (with fossils")
sd(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
print("Min of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (with fossils")
min(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)
print("Max of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP MOL and MP TE (with fossils")
max(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesMOL)

print("Median of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP TE (without fossils) and MP TE (with fossils")
median(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE)
print("SD of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP TE (without fossils) and MP TE (with fossils")
sd(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE)
print("Min of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP TE (without fossils) and MP TE (with fossils")
min(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE)
print("Max of paired differences in number of polytomies between MP TE (without fossils) and MP TE (with fossils")
max(df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct - df_reduced$MP_nPolytomiesTE)

# 6. Statistical inference (Table S6)
df_friedman <- df_wide %>% 
  select(MP_nPolytomiesMOL, MP_nPolytomiesTE, MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct)
# Friedman test
friedman_test <- friedman.test(as.matrix(df_friedman))
friedman_test
# Posthoc Wilcoxon
# Add row ID for pairing
df_plot <- df_wide %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number())
# Convert to long format
df_long <- df_plot %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(MP_nPolytomiesMOL, MP_nPolytomiesTE, MP_nPolytomiesTE_Extinct),
    names_to = "group",
    values_to = "value"
  )
pairwise.wilcox.test(df_long$value, df_long$group, 
                     paired = TRUE, 
                     p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")

# 7. FIGURE S8
```

## Q3.3 Contribution of morphological evidence to the TE optimality score

In addition to testing whether MOL-TE incongruences differ between optimaliy criteria, we can explore the impact of morphological evidence to optimality scores between optimality criteria. Specifically, it is possible that the MKv model can constrain the contribution of the morphological partition to the TE optimality score in ML, whereas the same does not occur in MP analyses. As such, we need to test whether the proportion of optimality scores between MORPH and TE is higher in MP than ML analyses.

### Q3.3.1 Extant (Figure 5 and S9)

```{r}
# Load data for extant taxa
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
df_extant <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extant", Type)) # keep only extant datasets
df_extant <- df_extant[!is.na(df_extant$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEnoASC_score), ]

# Option 1. PHEcost / TEcost
op1_mp = (df_extant$MP_MORPHonTE_Score) / (df_extant$MP_TE_Score)
op1_ml_mk = (df_extant$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEnoASC_score) / (df_extant$ML_TNT_TEnoASC_Score)
op1_ml_mkv = (df_extant$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEasc_score) / (df_extant$ML_TNT_TEasc_Score)

print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is higher in MP than ML MK")
sum(op1_mp > op1_ml_mk)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is lower in MP than ML MK")
sum(op1_mp < op1_ml_mk)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is equal in MP than ML MK")
sum(op1_mp == op1_ml_mk)

print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is higher in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op1_mp > op1_ml_mkv)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is lower in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op1_mp < op1_ml_mkv)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is equal in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op1_mp == op1_ml_mkv)

print("Stats MP")
mean(op1_mp)
sd(op1_mp)
min(op1_mp)
max(op1_mp)
print("Stats ML MK")
mean(op1_ml_mk)
sd(op1_ml_mk)
min(op1_ml_mk)
max(op1_ml_mk)
print("Stats ML MKv")
mean(op1_ml_mkv)
sd(op1_ml_mkv)
min(op1_ml_mkv)
max(op1_ml_mkv)

# Normality tests
shapiro.test(op1_mp) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(op1_ml_mk) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(op1_ml_mkv) # p < 0.05, non-parametric

# Friedman test (non-parametric, multiple groups, paired values)
op1_q3_fri = data.frame(op1_mp, op1_ml_mk, op1_ml_mkv)
friedman.test(as.matrix(op1_q3_fri))

# Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(op1_q3_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(op1_q3_fri), each = nrow(op1_q3_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

# Figure S9
# Compute counts (MP vs ML MKv)
n_lower_mkv <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp < op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mkv)
n_higher_mkv <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp > op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mkv)
n_equal_mkv  <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp == op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mkv)
# Compute counts (MP vs ML MK)
n_lower_mk <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp < op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mk)
n_higher_mk <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp > op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mk)
n_equal_mk  <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp == op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mk)
# Figure S9
cols <- c("op1_mp" = "#339999", "op1_ml_mkv" = "#6f77b4", "op1_ml_mk" = "#cccccc")
# Add row ID
op1_q3_fri$row_id <- 1:nrow(op1_q3_fri)
# Pre-compute jitter offsets (same seed) — smaller jitter
set.seed(42)
n <- nrow(op1_q3_fri)
jitter_offsets <- data.frame(
  row_id   = 1:n,
  jitter_1 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_2 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_3 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03)
)
# Merge offsets — new order: ML MKv, MP, ML MK (positions 1, 2, 3)
df_jitter <- op1_q3_fri %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(
    x1 = 1 + jitter_1,  # ML MKv
    x2 = 2 + jitter_2,  # MP
    x3 = 3 + jitter_3,  # ML MK
    seg1_color = case_when(
      op1_ml_mkv < op1_mp ~ "darkred",
      op1_ml_mkv > op1_mp ~ "blue",
      TRUE                ~ "gray"
    ),
    seg2_color = case_when(
      op1_mp > op1_ml_mk ~ "darkred",
      op1_mp < op1_ml_mk ~ "blue",
      TRUE               ~ "gray"
    )
  )
# Convert to long format — new level order
df_long <- op1_q3_fri %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(op1_ml_mkv, op1_mp, op1_ml_mk),
               names_to  = "group",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("op1_ml_mkv", "op1_mp", "op1_ml_mk"))) %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(x_jittered = case_when(
    group == "op1_ml_mkv" ~ 1 + jitter_1,
    group == "op1_mp"     ~ 2 + jitter_2,
    group == "op1_ml_mk"  ~ 3 + jitter_3
  ))
# Plot
op1_plot = ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(data = df_long,
               aes(x = as.numeric(group), y = value, fill = group),
               alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA,
               color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5, width = 0.5) +
  # Segments: ML MKv -> MP
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = op1_ml_mkv, yend = op1_mp, color = seg1_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  # Segments: MP -> ML MK
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,

      "MP vs ML MK  — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mk,  "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mk,  "  equal: ", n_equal_mk
    )
  ) +
```

```{r}
# Normality tests

# Friedman test (non-parametric, multiple groups, paired values)
op3_q3_fri = data.frame(op3_mp, op3_ml_mk, op3_ml_mkv)
friedman.test(as.matrix(op3_q3_fri))

# Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(op3_q3_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(op3_q3_fri), each = nrow(op3_q3_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")


# Compute counts (MP vs ML MKv)
n_lower_mkv <- sum(op3_q3_fri$op3_mp < op3_q3_fri$op3_ml_mkv)
n_higher_mkv <- sum(op3_q3_fri$op3_mp > op3_q3_fri$op3_ml_mkv)
n_equal_mkv  <- sum(op3_q3_fri$op3_mp == op3_q3_fri$op3_ml_mkv)
# Compute counts (MP vs ML MK)
n_lower_mk <- sum(op3_q3_fri$op3_mp < op3_q3_fri$op3_ml_mk)
n_higher_mk <- sum(op3_q3_fri$op3_mp > op3_q3_fri$op3_ml_mk)
n_equal_mk  <- sum(op3_q3_fri$op3_mp == op3_q3_fri$op3_ml_mk)
# Figure S9
cols <- c("op3_mp" = "#339999", "op3_ml_mkv" = "#6f77b4", "op3_ml_mk" = "#cccccc")
# Add row ID
op3_q3_fri$row_id <- 1:nrow(op3_q3_fri)
# Pre-compute jitter offsets (same seed) — smaller jitter
set.seed(42)
n <- nrow(op3_q3_fri)
jitter_offsets <- data.frame(
  row_id   = 1:n,
  jitter_1 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_2 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_3 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03)
)
# Merge offsets — new order: ML MKv, MP, ML MK (positions 1, 2, 3)
df_jitter <- op3_q3_fri %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(
    x1 = 1 + jitter_1,  # ML MKv
    x2 = 2 + jitter_2,  # MP
    x3 = 3 + jitter_3,  # ML MK
    seg1_color = case_when(
      op3_ml_mkv < op3_mp ~ "darkred",
      op3_ml_mkv > op3_mp ~ "blue",
      TRUE                ~ "gray"
    ),
    seg2_color = case_when(
      op3_mp > op3_ml_mk ~ "darkred",
      op3_mp < op3_ml_mk ~ "blue",
      TRUE               ~ "gray"
    )
  )
# Convert to long format — new level order
df_long <- op3_q3_fri %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(op3_ml_mkv, op3_mp, op3_ml_mk),
               names_to  = "group",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("op3_ml_mkv", "op3_mp", "op3_ml_mk"))) %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(x_jittered = case_when(
    group == "op3_ml_mkv" ~ 1 + jitter_1,
    group == "op3_mp"     ~ 2 + jitter_2,
    group == "op3_ml_mk"  ~ 3 + jitter_3
  ))
# Plot
op3_plot=ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(data = df_long,
               aes(x = as.numeric(group), y = value, fill = group),
               alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA,
               color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5, width = 0.5) +
  # Segments: ML MKv -> MP
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = op3_ml_mkv, yend = op3_mp, color = seg1_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  # Segments: MP -> ML MK
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x2, xend = x3, y = op3_mp, yend = op3_ml_mk, color = seg2_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = df_long,
             aes(x = x_jittered, y = value, color = group),
             size = 2, alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(cols,
                                "darkred"  = "darkred",
                                "blue" = "blue",
                                "gray" = "gray70")) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x    = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = expression("(PHE"["cost"] ~ "-" ~ "PHE"["homoplasy"] ~ ")" ~ "/" ~ "(TE"["cost"] ~ "-" ~ "TE"["homoplasy"] ~ ")")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3,
                     labels = c("ML MKv", "MP", "ML MK"))+
  labs(
    y       = expression("(PHE"["cost"] ~ "-" ~ "PHE"["homoplasy"] ~ ")" ~ "/" ~ "(TE"["cost"] ~ "-" ~ "TE"["homoplasy"] ~ ")"),
    caption = paste0(
      "MP vs ML MKv — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mkv, "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mkv, "  equal: ", n_equal_mkv, "\n",
      "MP vs ML MK  — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mk,  "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mk,  "  equal: ", n_equal_mk
    )
  ) +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray40"))
```

### Q3.3.2 Extant + extinct

```{r}
# Load data
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")
#df_extinct <- df %>% filter(grepl("Extinct", Type)) # keep only extinct datasets
# Keep only extinct
extinct_datasets <- unique(df$Dataset[df$Type == "Extinct"])
# Append the extant datasets that do not appear among extinct
df_extinct <- df[df$Type == "Extinct" | 
                  (df$Type == "Extant" & !(df$Dataset %in% extinct_datasets)), ]

# Option 1. PHEcost / TEcost
op1_mp = (df_extinct$MP_MORPHonTE_Score) / (df_extinct$MP_TE_Score)
op1_ml_mk = (df_extinct$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEnoASC_score) / (df_extinct$ML_TNT_TEnoASC_Score)
op1_ml_mkv = (df_extinct$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEasc_score) / (df_extinct$ML_TNT_TEasc_Score)

print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is higher in MP than ML MK")
sum(op1_mp > op1_ml_mk)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is lower in MP than ML MK")
sum(op1_mp < op1_ml_mk)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is equal in MP than ML MK")
sum(op1_mp == op1_ml_mk)

print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is higher in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op1_mp > op1_ml_mkv)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is lower in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op1_mp < op1_ml_mkv)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is equal in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op1_mp == op1_ml_mkv)

print("Stats MP")
mean(op1_mp)
sd(op1_mp)
min(op1_mp)
max(op1_mp)
print("Stats ML MK")
mean(op1_ml_mk)
sd(op1_ml_mk)
min(op1_ml_mk)
max(op1_ml_mk)
print("Stats ML MKv")
mean(op1_ml_mkv)
sd(op1_ml_mkv)
min(op1_ml_mkv)
max(op1_ml_mkv)

# Normality tests
shapiro.test(op1_mp) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(op1_ml_mk) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(op1_ml_mkv) # p < 0.05, non-parametric

# Friedman test (non-parametric, multiple groups, paired values)
op1_q3_fri = data.frame(op1_mp, op1_ml_mk, op1_ml_mkv)
friedman.test(as.matrix(op1_q3_fri))

# Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(op1_q3_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(op1_q3_fri), each = nrow(op1_q3_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

# Figure S8
# Compute counts (MP vs ML MKv)
n_lower_mkv <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp < op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mkv)
n_higher_mkv <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp > op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mkv)
n_equal_mkv  <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp == op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mkv)
# Compute counts (MP vs ML MK)
n_lower_mk <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp < op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mk)
n_higher_mk <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp > op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mk)
n_equal_mk  <- sum(op1_q3_fri$op1_mp == op1_q3_fri$op1_ml_mk)
# Figure S5
cols <- c("op1_mp" = "#339999", "op1_ml_mkv" = "#6f77b4", "op1_ml_mk" = "#cccccc")
# Add row ID
op1_q3_fri$row_id <- 1:nrow(op1_q3_fri)
# Pre-compute jitter offsets (same seed) — smaller jitter
set.seed(42)
n <- nrow(op1_q3_fri)
jitter_offsets <- data.frame(
  row_id   = 1:n,
  jitter_1 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_2 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_3 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03)
)
# Merge offsets — new order: ML MKv, MP, ML MK (positions 1, 2, 3)
df_jitter <- op1_q3_fri %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(
    x1 = 1 + jitter_1,  # ML MKv
    x2 = 2 + jitter_2,  # MP
    x3 = 3 + jitter_3,  # ML MK
    seg1_color = case_when(
      op1_ml_mkv < op1_mp ~ "darkred",
      op1_ml_mkv > op1_mp ~ "blue",
      TRUE                ~ "gray"
    ),
    seg2_color = case_when(
      op1_mp > op1_ml_mk ~ "darkred",
      op1_mp < op1_ml_mk ~ "blue",
      TRUE               ~ "gray"
    )
  )
# Convert to long format — new level order
df_long <- op1_q3_fri %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(op1_ml_mkv, op1_mp, op1_ml_mk),
               names_to  = "group",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("op1_ml_mkv", "op1_mp", "op1_ml_mk"))) %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(x_jittered = case_when(
    group == "op1_ml_mkv" ~ 1 + jitter_1,
    group == "op1_mp"     ~ 2 + jitter_2,
    group == "op1_ml_mk"  ~ 3 + jitter_3
  ))
# Plot
op1_plot = ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(data = df_long,
               aes(x = as.numeric(group), y = value, fill = group),
               alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA,
               color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5, width = 0.5) +
  # Segments: ML MKv -> MP
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = op1_ml_mkv, yend = op1_mp, color = seg1_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  # Segments: MP -> ML MK
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x2, xend = x3, y = op1_mp, yend = op1_ml_mk, color = seg2_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = df_long,
             aes(x = x_jittered, y = value, color = group),
             size = 2, alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(cols,
                                "darkred"  = "darkred",
                                "blue" = "blue",
                                "gray" = "gray70")) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x    = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = expression("PHE"["cost"] ~ "/" ~ "TE"["cost"] ~ "\n")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3,
                     labels = c("ML MKv", "MP", "ML MK"))+
  labs(
    y       = expression("PHE"["cost"] ~ "/" ~ "TE"["cost"] ~ "\n"),
    caption = paste0(
      "MP vs ML MKv — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mkv, "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mkv, "  equal: ", n_equal_mkv, "\n",
      "MP vs ML MK  — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mk,  "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mk,  "  equal: ", n_equal_mk
    )
  ) +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray40"))

op1_plot
```

```{r}
sum(op5_mp < op5_ml_mkv)
print("Number of times that contribution of PHE is equal in MP than ML MKv")
sum(op5_mp == op5_ml_mkv)

print("Stats MP")
mean(op5_mp)
sd(op5_mp)
min(op5_mp)
max(op5_mp)
print("Stats ML MK")
mean(op5_ml_mk)
sd(op5_ml_mk)
min(op5_ml_mk)
max(op5_ml_mk)
print("Stats ML MKv")
mean(op5_ml_mkv)
sd(op5_ml_mkv)
min(op5_ml_mkv)
max(op5_ml_mkv)

# Normality tests
shapiro.test(op5_mp) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(op5_ml_mk) # p < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(op5_ml_mkv) # p < 0.05, non-parametric

# Friedman test (non-parametric, multiple groups, paired values)
op5_q3_fri <- data.frame(op5_mp, op5_ml_mk, op5_ml_mkv) %>%
  filter(is.finite(op5_mp) & is.finite(op5_ml_mk) & is.finite(op5_ml_mkv))
friedman.test(as.matrix(op5_q3_fri))

# Wilcoxon: pairwise comparisons for paired values
pairwise.wilcox.test(x=unlist(op5_q3_fri),
                     g=factor(base::rep(names(op5_q3_fri), each = nrow(op5_q3_fri))),
                     paired=TRUE,
                     p.adjust.method="bonferroni")

# Compute counts (MP vs ML MKv)
n_lower_mkv <- sum(op5_q3_fri$op5_mp < op5_q3_fri$op5_ml_mkv)
n_higher_mkv <- sum(op5_q3_fri$op5_mp > op5_q3_fri$op5_ml_mkv)
n_equal_mkv  <- sum(op5_q3_fri$op5_mp == op5_q3_fri$op5_ml_mkv)
# Compute counts (MP vs ML MK)
n_lower_mk <- sum(op5_q3_fri$op5_mp < op5_q3_fri$op5_ml_mk)
n_higher_mk <- sum(op5_q3_fri$op5_mp > op5_q3_fri$op5_ml_mk)
n_equal_mk  <- sum(op5_q3_fri$op5_mp == op5_q3_fri$op5_ml_mk)
# Figure S5
cols <- c("op5_mp" = "#339999", "op5_ml_mkv" = "#6f77b4", "op5_ml_mk" = "#cccccc")
# Add row ID
op5_q3_fri$row_id <- 1:nrow(op5_q3_fri)
# Pre-compute jitter offsets (same seed) — smaller jitter
set.seed(42)
n <- nrow(op5_q3_fri)
jitter_offsets <- data.frame(
  row_id   = 1:n,
  jitter_1 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_2 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03),
  jitter_3 = runif(n, -0.03, 0.03)
)
# Merge offsets — new order: ML MKv, MP, ML MK (positions 1, 2, 3)
df_jitter <- op5_q3_fri %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(
    x1 = 1 + jitter_1,  # ML MKv
    x2 = 2 + jitter_2,  # MP
    x3 = 3 + jitter_3,  # ML MK
    seg1_color = case_when(
      op5_ml_mkv < op5_mp ~ "darkred",
      op5_ml_mkv > op5_mp ~ "blue",
      TRUE                ~ "gray"
    ),
    seg2_color = case_when(
      op5_mp > op5_ml_mk ~ "darkred",
      op5_mp < op5_ml_mk ~ "blue",
      TRUE               ~ "gray"
    )
  )
# Convert to long format — new level order
df_long <- op5_q3_fri %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(op5_ml_mkv, op5_mp, op5_ml_mk),
               names_to  = "group",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("op5_ml_mkv", "op5_mp", "op5_ml_mk"))) %>%
  left_join(jitter_offsets, by = "row_id") %>%
  mutate(x_jittered = case_when(
    group == "op5_ml_mkv" ~ 1 + jitter_1,
    group == "op5_mp"     ~ 2 + jitter_2,
    group == "op5_ml_mk"  ~ 3 + jitter_3
  ))
# Plot
op5_plot=ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(data = df_long,
               aes(x = as.numeric(group), y = value, fill = group),
               alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA,
               color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5, width = 0.5) +
  # Segments: ML MKv -> MP
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = op5_ml_mkv, yend = op5_mp, color = seg1_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  # Segments: MP -> ML MK
  geom_segment(data = df_jitter,
               aes(x = x2, xend = x3, y = op5_mp, yend = op5_ml_mk, color = seg2_color),
               linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = df_long,
             aes(x = x_jittered, y = value, color = group),
             size = 2, alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(cols,
                                "darkred"  = "darkred",
                                "blue" = "blue",
                                "gray" = "gray70")) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x    = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = expression("(PHE"["cost"] ~ "x" ~ "PHE"["CI"] ~ ")" ~ "/" ~ "(TE"["cost"]) ~ "x" ~ "TE"["CI"]~ ")") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3,
                     labels = c("ML MKv", "MP", "ML MK"))+
  labs(  y       = expression("(PHE"["cost"] ~ "x" ~ "PHE"["CI"] ~ ")" ~ "/" ~ "(TE"["cost"] ~ "x" ~ "TE"["CI"] ~ ")"),
         caption = paste0(
      "MP vs ML MKv — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mkv, "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mkv, "  equal: ", n_equal_mkv, "\n",
      "MP vs ML MK  — lower in MP: ", n_lower_mk,  "  higher in MP: ", n_higher_mk,  "  equal: ", n_equal_mk
    )
  ) +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray40"))

op5_plot
```

### Q3.3.3 Size analyses (Figure S10)

```{r}
# Contribution of morphology between NGS and Sanger

# Load data for extant taxa
df <- read.csv("Dataset_R_q123_07-26.csv")

# Option 1. PHEcost / TEcost
op1_mp = (df$MP_MORPHonTE_Score) / (df$MP_TE_Score)
op1_ml_mk = (df$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEnoASC_score) / (df$ML_TNT_TEnoASC_Score)
op1_ml_mkv = (df$ML_TNT_MORPHonTEasc_score) / (df$ML_TNT_TEasc_Score)

op1_q3 = data.frame(op1_mp, op1_ml_mk, op1_ml_mkv)
# Add row ID
op1_q3$row_id <- 1:nrow(op1_q3)
# Add NGS x Sanger
op1_q3$sequencing = df$Sequencing
# Add Extant x Extinct
op1_q3$taxa = df$Type
# Add %Morphological characters
op1_q3$percentageMorphCharacters = df$X.Morph.Total

# Convert to long format
df_long <- op1_q3 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(op1_mp, op1_ml_mk, op1_ml_mkv),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Method = factor(
      Method,
      levels = c("op1_mp", "op1_ml_mk", "op1_ml_mkv"),
      labels = c("MP", "ML-Mk", "ML-MkV")
    )
  )

# Plot
figs9 = ggplot(df_long, aes(x = sequencing, y = Value, fill = sequencing)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.2,
    color = "gray"
  ) +
  stat_compare_means(
  comparisons = list(c("Sanger", "NGS")),
  method = "wilcox.test",
  paired = F,
  label = "p.format",
  label.y = max(df_long$Value, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05, bracket.size = 0
) +
  facet_wrap(~Method, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Sanger" = "#4E79A7",
    "NGS" = "#E15759"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Morphological score / TE score\n"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "plain")
  )
```

# Q4. How do bootstrap values of shared clades differ between MOL and TE trees? 

## Q4.1 Unique vs Shared 

### Q4.2 With and without fossils (Table 2 and S7, Figure 8)

Before testing the differences of BS values in shared clades between MOL and TE trees, let's explore the differences of BS values between shared and unique clades.

First, we need to format the extant datasets.

```{r}
# Load shared clades
df_shared = read.csv ("/Users/labanfibios/Desktop/Doutorado/Project/B2_TEvsMOL/GitHub/Dataset_R_q4_07-26_shared.csv")
# Load unique clades
df_unique = read.csv ("/Users/labanfibios/Desktop/Doutorado/Project/B2_TEvsMOL/GitHub/Dataset_R_q4_07-26_unique.csv")

# Rename the column Analysis to Dataset
df_unique <- df_unique %>% 
  rename(Dataset = Analysis)
# Rename the column Method to Optimality
df_unique <- df_unique %>% 
  rename(Optimality = Method)
# Rename the column Type to Analysis
df_unique <- df_unique %>% 
  rename(Analysis = Type)
# Create a new column called Type (unique vs shared)
df_unique <- df_unique %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Type = "unique")

# Create a new dataframe from df_shared with the selected columns
df_shared_stack <- df_shared %>%
  transmute(
    Dataset = Dataset,
    Analysis = "MOL",                 # new value
    Optimality = Optimality,
    Node = Node_Tree_1,               # take Node_Tree_1
    Support = Support_Tree_1,         # take Support_Tree_1
    Type = "shared"                   # new value
  )
# Bind the new rows below df_unique
df_unique_extended <- bind_rows(df_unique, df_shared_stack)
# Create a new dataframe from df_shared for Tree 2
df_shared_stack2 <- df_shared %>%
  transmute(
    Dataset = Dataset,
    Analysis = "TE",                  # new value for Tree 2
    Optimality = Optimality,
    Node = Node_Tree_2,               # take Node_Tree_2
    Support = Support_Tree_2,         # take Support_Tree_2
    Type = "shared"                   # new value
  )
# Append Tree 2 rows to df_unique_extended (which already contains Tree 1 and unique rows)
df_uniqueVSshared <- bind_rows(df_unique_extended, df_shared_stack2)

# Rename
df_uniqueVSshared <- df_uniqueVSshared %>%
  mutate(
    Optimality = recode(
      Optimality,
      "ML-ASC" = "ML_ASC",
      "ML-noASC" = "ML_noASC"
    )
  )
# Add the column Sampling (without fossils vs with fossils)
df_uniqueVSshared <- df_uniqueVSshared %>%
  mutate(Sampling = "Without_fossils")

#View(df_uniqueVSshared)
```

```{r}
    n = n(),

    sd_support = sd(Support, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

We can statistically test whether bootstrap values differ between shared and unique clades, considering Type (categorical predictor: unique vs shared), Sampling (categorical predictor: Without_fossils vs With_fossils), Optimality (categorical predictor: MP vs ML_ASC vs ML_noASC), Analysis (categorical predictor: MOL vs TE). We will use both traditional non-parametric tests and GLMs.

```{r}
# Fix: Squeeze Support into (0,1) for GLMM with Beta distribution
df_combined <- df_combined %>%
  mutate(Support_beta = (Support + 0.5) / 101) 

# Fix: Squeeze Support into (0,1) for GLMM with Beta distribution
df_extinct_63 <- df_extinct_63 %>%
  mutate(Support_beta = (Support + 0.5) / 101) 

# Split datasets
df_without <- df_combined %>% filter(Sampling == "Without_fossils")
df_with    <- df_combined %>% filter(Sampling == "With_fossils")

# --- Helper function for classical non-parametric tests ---
run_nonparametric_tests <- function(df) {
  results <- list()
  
  # 1. Kruskal-Wallis for Type, Optimality, Analysis
  results$kw_type <- kruskal_test(df, Support ~ Type)
  results$kw_opt  <- kruskal_test(df, Support ~ Optimality)
  results$kw_an   <- kruskal_test(df, Support ~ Analysis)
  
  # 2. Pairwise Wilcoxon for Type by Optimality & Analysis
  pw_list <- list()
  
  for(opt in unique(df$Optimality)){
    for(an in unique(df$Analysis)){
      subset_df <- df %>% filter(Optimality == opt, Analysis == an)
      test_res <- pairwise_wilcox_test(
        subset_df,
        Support ~ Type,
        p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
      )
      test_res <- test_res %>% mutate(Optimality = opt, Analysis = an)
      pw_list[[paste(opt, an, sep = "_")]] <- test_res
    }
  }
  
  results$pairwise <- bind_rows(pw_list)
  return(results)
}

# Function to summarize mean, sd, min, max
summarize_support <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(Optimality, Analysis, Type) %>%
    summarise(
      n    = n(),
      mean = mean(Support, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd   = sd(Support, na.rm = TRUE),
      min  = min(Support, na.rm = TRUE),
      max  = max(Support, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# All combinations to test
combinations <- expand.grid(
  Optimality = c("MP", "ML MK", "ML MKv"),
  Analysis = c("MOL", "TE"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Function to run pairwise GLMM for one subset
run_pairwise <- function(df_subset) {
  results <- list()
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(combinations)) {
    opt <- combinations$Optimality[i]
    ana <- combinations$Analysis[i]
    
    df_sub <- df_subset %>%
      filter(Optimality == opt, Analysis == ana)
    
    if (nrow(df_sub) > 0) {
      # Fit beta GLMM
      glmm <- glmmTMB(
        Support_beta ~ Type + (1|Dataset),
        family = beta_family(link = "logit"),
        data = df_sub
      )
      
      # Pairwise comparisons for Type
      em <- emmeans(glmm, ~ Type)
      pw <- pairs(em, adjust = "bonferroni")
      
      results[[paste(opt, ana, sep = "_")]] <- summary(pw)
    }
  }
  
  bind_rows(results, .id = "Comparison")
}

run_pairwise_df <- function(df_subset, combinations_df, rand = "(1|Dataset)") {
  out_list <- list()
  for(i in seq_len(nrow(combinations_df))) {
    opt <- combinations_df$Optimality[i]
    ana <- combinations_df$Analysis[i]
    df_sub <- df_subset %>% filter(Optimality == opt, Analysis == ana)
    
    # need at least two Type levels and some rows
    if(nrow(df_sub) < 4 || length(unique(df_sub$Type)) < 2) {
      warning(sprintf("Skipping %s_%s: insufficient data (n=%d, types=%s)",
                      opt, ana, nrow(df_sub), paste(unique(df_sub$Type), collapse=", ")))
      next
    }
    
    # Fit model safely
    glmm <- try(
      glmmTMB(Support_beta ~ Type + (1|Dataset), data = df_sub, family = beta_family(link="logit")),
      silent = TRUE
    )
    if(inherits(glmm, "try-error")) {
      warning(sprintf("Model failed for %s_%s: %s", opt, ana, attr(glmm, "condition")$message))
      next
    }
    
    # emmeans and pairwise contrasts
    em <- try(emmeans(glmm, ~ Type), silent = TRUE)
    if(inherits(em, "try-error")) {
      warning(sprintf("emmeans failed for %s_%s", opt, ana))
      next
    }
    pw <- try(pairs(em, adjust = "bonferroni"), silent = TRUE)
    if(inherits(pw, "try-error")) {
      warning(sprintf("pairs() failed for %s_%s", opt, ana))
      next
    }
    
    # convert to data.frame to get exact numeric p-values
    pw_df <- as.data.frame(pw)
    # add context columns
    pw_df <- pw_df %>%
      mutate(
        Optimality = opt,
        Analysis   = ana,
        Comparison = rownames(pw_df)  # usually "unique - shared" or similar
      ) %>%
      select(Optimality, Analysis, Comparison, everything())
    
    out_list[[paste(opt, ana, sep = "_")]] <- pw_df
  }
  
  if(length(out_list) == 0) return(tibble()) 
  res <- bind_rows(out_list, .id = "id")
  
  # Add nicely formatted p-values:
  res <- res %>%
    mutate(
      p.value_numeric = as.numeric(p.value),
      p.value_fmt = ifelse(
        is.na(p.value_numeric), NA,
        ifelse(p.value_numeric < 0.001,
               formatC(p.value_numeric, format = "e", digits = 2),           # scientific for <0.001
               formatC(p.value_numeric, format = "f", digits = 3))           # 3 decimals otherwise
    ))
  
  return(res)
}

```

## Q4.2 MOL vs TE (Table 5)

### Q4.2.1 Extant

First, we need to load the data. Support values of shared clades were identified and organized using the package RNODE. 

```{r}
# Load data (BS shared clades)
df_q4 = read.csv("Dataset_R_q4_07-26_shared.csv")

# Set order of optimality criteria
df_q4$Optimality <- factor(df_q4$Optimality, levels = c("MP", "ML-ASC", "ML-noASC"))
df_q4$SupportDiff = df_q4$Support_Tree_1 - df_q4$Support_Tree_2
```

For each optimality criterion, we tested whether the paired values of bootstrap of shared clades differ between MOL and TE trees. First, we computed the number of clades in which bootstrap values were the same in MOL and TE trees, higher in MOL than TE trees, or higher in TE than MOL trees. Next, we tested the normality of bootstrap values using Shapiro-Wilk tests. Finally, we used both the non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank and Generalized Linear Mixed Models.

```{r}
                           paired = TRUE)

# Dataset for GLMMs
df_MP_glmm <- data.frame(
  Node = c(df_MP$Node_Tree_1, df_MP$Node_Tree_2),
  Approach = c(df_MP$Approach1, df_MP$Approach2),
  Support = c(df_MP$Support_Tree_1, df_MP$Support_Tree_2),
  ID = c(df_MP$ID, df_MP$ID)
)

# GLMM Beta
# Step 1. Scale Support from 0–100 to 0–1
df_MP_glmm <- df_MP_glmm %>%
  mutate(Support_prop = Support / 100)
# Beta regression does not allow exact 0 or 1
n <- nrow(df_MP_glmm)
df_MP_glmm <- df_MP_glmm %>%
  mutate(Support_beta = (Support_prop * (n - 1) + 0.5) / n)
mp_beta <- glmmTMB(Support_beta ~ Approach + (1 | ID),
                 family = beta_family(link = "logit"),
                 data = df_MP_glmm)
summary(mp_beta)
```

### Q4.2.2 Extant + extinct

First, we need to load the data including fossils. Support values of shared clades were identified and organized using the package RNODE. 

```{r}
# Load data (BS shared clades)
df_q4 = read.csv("Dataset_R_q4_09-25_shared_extinct.csv")

# Set order of optimality criteria
df_q4$Optimality <- factor(df_q4$Optimality, levels = c("MP", "ML-ASC", "ML-noASC"))
df_q4$SupportDiff = df_q4$Support_Tree_1 - df_q4$Support_Tree_2

# The names of the datasets are 1 .. 2. We need to corrected them to the original names
map <- c(
  "1"=3, "2"=7, "3"=8, "4"=9, "5"=10, "6"=11, "7"=13, "8"=17, "9"=21,
  "10"=24, "11"=28, "12"=29, "13"=31, "14"=38, "15"=39, "16"=40,
  "17"=42, "18"=46, "19"=48, "20"=52, "21"=54, "22"=58
)
df_q4$Dataset <- map[as.character(df_q4$Dataset)]

# Correct the values in df_q4$ID
df_q4$ID <- paste0(
  map[sub("_.*","", df_q4$ID)],
  sub("^[^_]+","", df_q4$ID)
)

# Include the datasets of extant organisms, without duplications
df_q4_extant = read.csv("Dataset_R_q4_07-26_shared.csv")
df_q4_extant$Optimality <- factor(df_q4_extant$Optimality, levels = c("MP", "ML-ASC", "ML-noASC"))
df_q4_extant$SupportDiff = df_q4_extant$Support_Tree_1 - df_q4_extant$Support_Tree_2
df_q4 <- bind_rows(
  df_q4,
  anti_join(df_q4_extant, df_q4, by = "ID")
)

```

```{r}
# Shapiro-Wilk test for normality
shapiro.test(df_MP$Support_Tree_1) # P < 0.05, non-parametric
shapiro.test(df_MP$Support_Tree_2) # P < 0.05, non-parametric

# Perform the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired values
wilcox.test(as.numeric(df_MP$Support_Tree_1),
                           as.numeric(df_MP$Support_Tree_2),
                           paired = TRUE)

# Dataset for GLMMs
df_MP_glmm_f <- data.frame(
  Node = c(df_MP$Node_Tree_1, df_MP$Node_Tree_2),
  Approach = c(df_MP$Approach1, df_MP$Approach2),
  Support = c(df_MP$Support_Tree_1, df_MP$Support_Tree_2),
  ID = c(df_MP$ID, df_MP$ID)
)

# GLMM Beta
# Step 1. Scale Support from 0–100 to 0–1
df_MP_glmm_f <- df_MP_glmm_f %>%
  mutate(Support_prop = Support / 100)
# Beta regression does not allow exact 0 or 1
n <- nrow(df_MP_glmm_f)
df_MP_glmm_f <- df_MP_glmm_f %>%
  mutate(Support_beta = (Support_prop * (n - 1) + 0.5) / n)
mp_beta <- glmmTMB(Support_beta ~ Approach + (1 | ID),
                 family = beta_family(link = "logit"),
                 data = df_MP_glmm_f)
summary(mp_beta)
```

### Q4.2.3 Plot (Figure S12)

First, we will plot the Figure 5A-C (without fossils).

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Create a new column with the optimality criterion
df_MP_glmm$comparison = "MPmol_MPte"
df_MLASC_glmm$comparison = "MLmol_MLteAsc"
df_MLnoASC_glmm$comparison = "MLmol_MLteNoAsc"

# Merge all comparisons into the same dataset
df_plot = bind_rows(df_MP_glmm, df_MLASC_glmm, df_MLnoASC_glmm)
#View(df_plot)

# Set order of comparisons
df_plot$comparison <- factor(df_plot$comparison, levels = c("MPmol_MPte", "MLmol_MLteAsc", "MLmol_MLteNoAsc"))
df_plot = df_plot[!is.na(df_plot$comparison), ]

# Set colors
custom_palette <- c("MPmol_MPte" = "#339999", "MLmol_MLteAsc" = "#6f77b4", "MLmol_MLteNoAsc" = "#cccccc")
# Create custom legend labels
custom_labels <- c(
  "MPmol_MPte" = "MP-MOL vs MP-TE",
  "MLmol_MLteAsc" = "ML-MOL vs ML-TE (with ASC)",
  "MLmol_MLteNoAsc" = "ML-MOL vs ML-TE (without ASC)"
)

# Box Plot MP
plot_mp = ggplot(df_MP_glmm, aes(x = Approach, y = Support)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  # Create boxplot without default outliers
  geom_jitter(color = "#339999", alpha = .04, width = 0.2) +  # Add transparent dots
  labs(x = "", y = "\nBootstrap\n", tag="A") +
  theme_minimal() +
  #theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +  # Hide legend if not needed
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels)
# Box Plot ML ASC
plot_ml_asc = ggplot(df_MLASC_glmm, aes(x = Approach, y = Support)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  # Create boxplot without default outliers
  geom_jitter(color = "#6f77b4", alpha = .04, width = 0.2) +  # Add transparent dots
  labs(x = "", y = "\nBootstrap\n", tag="B") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(50, NA)) + # Define o mínimo para 50, o máximo será ajustado automaticamente
  #theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +  # Hide legend if not needed
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels)
# Box Plot ML noASC
plot_ml_noasc = ggplot(df_MLnoASC_glmm, aes(x = Approach, y = Support)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  # Create boxplot without default outliers
  geom_jitter(color = "#cccccc", alpha = .07, width = 0.2) +  # Add transparent dots
  labs(x = "", y = "\nBootstrap\n", tag="C") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(50, NA)) + # Define o mínimo para 50, o máximo será ajustado automaticamente
  #theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") +  # Hide legend if not needed
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels)

# Extract the legend as a separate ggplot object
legend <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = comparison, y = Support, color = comparison)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette, labels = custom_labels) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
  )+
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha=.7)))  # Increase dot size in legend
# Convert the plot to a grob
plot_grob <- ggplotGrob(legend)
# Extract the legend from the grob
legend_grob <- gtable::gtable_filter(plot_grob, "guide-box")

# Plot 2x2
jpeg("Figures/FigS12ABC.jpg", width = 2000, height = 1600, res = 300)
grid.arrange(arrangeGrob(plot_mp + theme(plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,.01)),
                         plot_ml_asc + theme(plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,.01)),
                         plot_ml_noasc + theme(plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,.01)),
                         nrow=1, ncol=3),
             legend_grob,
             nrow=2,
             heights= c(20,1))
dev.off()
```
